Accessibility statement

Leoside Equity is built so that anyone can read it, whether they use a keyboard, a screen reader, magnification, voice control or a phone.

Last reviewed 28 September 2026

Contents

  1. The standard we work to

1. The standard we work to

Leoside Equity is built to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) version 2.2 at level AA. Content that meets version 2.2 at that level also meets version 2.1 AA, the level that accessibility rules in the United Kingdom, the European Union, India and the United States refer to. Version 2.2 adds six more requirements at level AA.

2. Conformance status

The site is partially conformant with WCAG 2.2 AA. This is the W3C's own term for a site where some content may not fully meet the standard. The parts we know of are listed in section 6, and each one has another way to get the same information.

3. What is built in

Keyboard
Everything works without a mouse, including menus, dialogs, search, the report filters and the globe on the home page, which turns with the arrow keys. Focus is always visible, and "Skip to content" is the first link on every page.
Structure
Every page has one main heading, headings in order, labelled regions, breadcrumbs, and its language set in the code.
Search
Press / or Ctrl K on any page to search reports and pages.
Colour and contrast
Body text is above 12 to 1 against its background in both themes, and secondary text above 4.5 to 1. Colour is never the only way something is shown: every market colour sits next to the market's name.
Light and dark themes
The site follows your system setting, and a switch in the header changes it.
Movement

The strip of company names on the home page stops when you point at it or move focus into it, and has a pause button. The cover of the latest report opens only while a mouse pointer rests on it and closes when the pointer leaves. Everything it shows is also on the report page.

Earlier reports on the home page are cards that stack up as you scroll. They move only when you scroll, and when one of them has keyboard focus the page scrolls so that it is not covered by the next. On short screens they sit in a plain column. With "reduce motion" switched on in your system, nothing moves on its own and the cover opens without animation.

New reports
If a report is published while the home page is open, the page adds it and says so in a short message that screen readers read out. It waits while your pointer or keyboard focus is on the reports, so nothing changes under you.
Text size and zoom
Text can be enlarged to 200 percent, and pages reflow to a single column down to 320 pixels wide without scrolling sideways.
Forms
Every field has a visible label. Errors are described in words, linked to the field, and announced to screen readers. The date of birth question uses three separate menus for day, month and year. Passwords can be shown while typing.
Time and flashing
There are no time limits on reading, and nothing flashes.
Printing
Reports and legal pages print in black on white, with link addresses written out.

4. How the site is assessed

The site is assessed by self-evaluation, one of the methods the W3C describes for accessibility statements. The last full assessment, on 25 September 2026, covered:

  • an automated audit of the main pages with Google Lighthouse in Chrome, with every problem it found fixed
  • keyboard walkthroughs of the main journeys: reading a report, searching, filtering the archive, signing up, signing in, and opening and closing every menu and dialog
  • layout at 320 pixels wide and at 200 percent zoom
  • reduced motion switched on, in the light theme and in the dark one

The stack of report cards added to the home page on 28 September 2026 was checked with the keyboard, at 320 pixels wide, and in both themes. It has no animation, so the reduced motion setting has nothing to turn off.

5. Browsers and technology

The site supports current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on computers and phones. Its accessibility relies on HTML, WAI-ARIA, CSS and JavaScript working in your browser.

6. Known limitations

The globe on the home page
It is an illustration. What it shows, the local time at each exchange and whether its regular session is open, is also written out in the list directly below it.
Google sign in
It takes you to a page run by Google, and that page's accessibility is Google's responsibility. Signing up with an email address works on this site without it.
Account emails
They are a single column of text with one clearly labelled link, which suits screen readers and text only mail programs. How they look depends on your mail program; tell us if one is hard to use.

7. Reporting a problem

If something on the site is hard to use, or you need a report in a different format, write to support@leosideequity.com with "Accessibility" in the subject. Tell us the page and what went wrong. We aim to reply within five working days, and will send the content in another format where we can.

8. If you are not satisfied

If you are not happy with our reply, you can contact the body that deals with accessibility complaints where you live. In the United Kingdom that is the Equality Advisory and Support Service; in the European Union, the national enforcement body for your country; in India, the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.

This statement was first prepared on 25 September 2026 and was last reviewed on 28 September 2026.
